responses.text: I wasn't aware of the zotero://plugin-schema, I just used the Zotero Plugin Template (https://github.com/windingwind/zotero-plugin-template), which enables this behavior for hot reloading, I think.
responses.reply: You're right that it comes from the template, and the card credits both links to zotero-plugin-toolkit, not to your own code. They aren't only for development, though: toolkit 5.x registers both zotero:// handlers whenever the plugin starts, in release builds too, so the finding holds for the released file. Toolkit 6.0.0 fixes it: zotero://plugin is gone, and the debug link is registered only if a plugin asks for it. Since you've retired the plugin, there's nothing to rebuild.

responses.text: This plugin does not work anymore. This is because you can't access the RI Opac using headless browsers. Please use https://github.com/theRatramnus/riopac-add-chapter-chrome instead.
responses.reply: Thanks for letting us know. The plugin is now marked as retired by its developer: it's out of our lists, this page says why and points to the Chrome extension, and we no longer offer it for install.

retired.reason: It no longer works: the RI OPAC can't be reached from headless browsers any more.
